newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran South Pars gasfield seen on stream in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Iran South Pars gasfield seen on stream in 1999.

text.p: The first phase development of Iran's massive South Pars gas and condensate field will come on stream in the second half of 1999, an Iranian official said on Monday.
Mostafa Khoei, managing director of the state-owned Petroleum Engineering and Development Company, was speaking at a gas conference.

Output of one billion cubic feet a day of gas will be used for domestic consumption. Future development of the field, 100 km (60 miles) from the Iranian coast, is essential to Iran's plans to export gas to Pakistan, India, Turkey and Europe in the next decade.
Phase one of the scheme is being handled by the Petroleum Development & Engineering Company (Pedec), a subsidiary of the national Iranian Oil Company (NOIC).
The NIOC has been in talks with a consortium led by Royal Dutch/Shell Group for the second phase development involving an additional one billion cubic feet a day of gas output.
France's Total recently said it was weighing the options of investing in the South Pars project.

South Pars is an extension in Iranian waters of Qatar's North Field. The newsletter Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) said recently that the National Iranian Oil Co's (NIOC) offshore arm expected to revise estimates of the field's gas reserves to perhaps as much as 500 trillion cubic feet.
